title: Memory orchestration gap analysis for serving: weights vs KV vs activations
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Production serving nodes intermittently hit OOMs during mixed traffic workloads where large model weights, aggressive KV caching, and variable activation peaks coincide. Current allocator treats weights as fixed and overcommits remaining GPU memory to KV/activations using conservative soft limits. We lack a clear budget split and runtime signals to dynamically reclaim headroom before OOMs occur.

Goal: Produce an actionable memory orchestration plan that defines explicit GPU memory budgets (weights, persistent KV, ephemeral activations), a headroom calculation for safe burst handling, and runtime signals + policies for preemptive KV eviction or activation offload. Deliverables: a) a gap analysis doc, b) proposed budget model and heuristics, c) simulator results demonstrating reduced OOM rate and acceptable latency cost, d) an RFC + rollout plan for a staged deployment (canary -> fleet).
acceptance_criteria: Clear budget formula for weights:static_reservation + safety_margin expressed per model family
KV budget policy that allows prioritized eviction tiers and respects pinned prefix caches
Headroom signal defined (percent of free mem + predicted near-term activation trend) and demonstrable trigger thresholds
Simulator showing >=3x reduction in OOM incidence on recorded 2026-01 production trace without >10% tail latency regression
RFC reviewed by runtime and infra leads and a canary rollout runbook created
comments: 2026-02-25 | Asha Patel: Created ticket after two post-mortem incidents (incident IDs INC-2026-02-11-A, INC-2026-02-18-B). Initial hypothesis: KV caching is being overly aggressive on p99 burst paths and isn't being preempted in time by the allocator.

2026-02-28 | Marcus Lee: Ran baseline memory trace analysis on 2026-01-15 production logs. Observed common pattern: weight memory stable, KV occupancy grows during inference-heavy windows, and activations spike for long-context requests. Attached heatmap in Confluence.

2026-03-03 | Elena Kuznetsov (review): Suggest splitting KV into two logical tiers: hot prefix cache (non-evictable within short window) and soft cache (evictable under headroom pressure). Also request that we quantify bandwidth/latency cost of KV rehydration in simulator.

2026-03-05 | Marcus Lee: Added simple headroom heuristic: headroom = max(free_mem - activation_estimate_peak, min_headroom_bytes). Activation estimate uses rolling 95th percentile of recent activation deltas per model family. Simulator integrated this signal as a preemptive KV-eviction trigger.

2026-03-08 | Marcus Lee: Simulator run #7 on Jan 15 trace reduced OOMs from 12 -> 3 in a 24h window. Tail latency (p99) increased by 6% for a small subset of requests that required KV rehydration. Uploaded sim-report.html to S3.

2026-03-10 | Product review (Sofia Hernández): Ask to include cost-analysis: how much additional GPU footprint would be required to eliminate regressions vs. algorithmic eviction. Also check impacts on Dedicated customers with pinned model weights.

2026-03-12 | Marcus Lee: Draft RFC uploaded to Confluence (link above). Proposed rollout: 1) unit-tests and stress tests on CI, 2) canary on non-critical region (20 nodes) for 48 hours, 3) extend to 30% of serving fleet with telemetry gates, 4) global rollout if OOM rate reduction holds. Created PR #2147 for allocator change; needs two approvals.
